source.title: Collaborative Label Correction via Entropy Thresholding
source.authors: Hao Wu; Jiangchao Yao; Jiajie Wang; Yin-Ru Chen; Ya Zhang; Yan-Feng Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures prediction entropy during training on synthetically noisy labels to examine whether correct predictions emerge before incorrect ones; this is a different measure and setting from the claim versions' direct random-label fitting tests.
record.gate_note: The paper studies synthetic and real-world label noise, not completely random labelings, shuffled pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Table accuracy results compare noisy-label learning methods and do not report training error, so they are not rows for the listed versions. Figure 2 reports the entropy dynamics and counts used below.
record.test_reason: The method relies on early learning of signal followed by memorization of noise. Its own demonstrations measure prediction confidence, confidence-filtered correctness, test accuracy, and final feature clustering; none directly tracks learning clean versus corrupted training labels over time.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the entropy demonstration but omits the paper's main conclusion: entropy thresholding combined with collaborative label correction provides reliable supervision, retains more samples than sample selection, and improves robustness across noisy image and text datasets. The authors interpret the confidence dynamics as consistent with memorization effects.
record.recipe_differences: Uses entropy trends and label-noise experiments, including collaborative label correction; it does not reproduce the original studies' random-label fitting setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes the low-entropy prediction count as changing over training: incorrect low-entropy predictions increase later as training proceeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct predictions become confident sooner than incorrect predictions; confident incorrect predictions increase later.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under synthetic symmetric noise on CIFAR-10, prediction confidence develops earlier for ground-truth-correct predictions than for incorrect predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: Standard-model features cluster by noisy labels at the final visualization; the authors interpret this as fitting noisy supervision.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard training can produce feature representations organized around partially corrupted training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Section III.C and Figure 3 report baseline test accuracy increasing initially and subsequently decreasing under high pairwise noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization can deteriorate during continued training on noisy labels; this alone does not identify which noisy training labels are memorized.

record.problems: The entropy results are shown only in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The paper's entropy demonstration uses a synthetic noisy-label setting and does not test completely random labels.
record.rows_left_out: Table II, Table III, and Table IV report test accuracy across noisy-label conditions and methods, but do not report the training-error outcomes named in the claim versions. Figure 5 reports sample counts and label precision for selection methods, not the behavior named by these versions.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Relative time to fit true and random labels, and convergence time across corruption fractions.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit alongside steadily worsening test performance across corruption fractions from zero to complete randomization.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after their removal.
Direct temporal measurements distinguishing learning shared real-data patterns from memorizing assigned noisy or random training labels.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the reported qualitative trends, but confidence dynamics and final clustering do not directly establish the claim versions' fitting behavior. No verdict labels follow from these rows.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling experiment or training-error result.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or fit time by corruption fraction.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiments.
Although the paper tests multiple noisy-label settings, it does not report perfect training fit across corruption fractions together with steadily rising test error toward chance.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, or of generalization after removing them.

The paper tests entropy dynamics for correct versus incorrect predictions on a CIFAR-10 synthetic symmetric-noise experiment. It does not test completely random labels or compare real labels against random labels in a separate experiment.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average prediction entropy over training for correct predictions.
rows.value: Figure only; text says entropy of correct predictions decreases fast.
rows.note: Text describes the plotted trend but supplies no numeric values.
rows.check: Entropy of correct predictions measures confidence, not when clean training labels are learned relative to noisy labels.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average prediction entropy over training for incorrect predictions.
rows.value: Figure only; text says entropy of incorrect predictions decreases at a rather slow pace.
rows.note: Text says the entropy gap between correct and incorrect predictions first becomes larger and then narrows.
rows.check: Increasing confidence in incorrect predictions does not establish memorization of the assigned noisy training labels.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average prediction entropy over training across all predictions.
rows.value: Figure only; text says entropy of predictions generally decreases to zero.
rows.note: The paper gives this as a general description of the plotted training process.
rows.check: Overall entropy approaching zero establishes confident predictions, not correct fitting of training labels or the learning order in V6.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Counted correct low-entropy predictions over training.
rows.measure: Number of samples with low-entropy predictions
rows.value: Figure only; text says the number increases sharply and persists at a high level.
rows.note: The figure and accompanying text describe the trend without numeric values.
rows.check: Counts correct predictions passing a confidence threshold, without separating clean-label and corrupted-label training examples or measuring their fitting.

rows.subject: DNN
rows.operation_detail: Counted incorrect low-entropy predictions over training.
rows.measure: Number of samples with low-entropy predictions
rows.value: Figure only; text says the number remains at a low level for a period and then increases as training proceeds.
rows.note: The increase later in training qualifies the period during which incorrect predictions remain uncommon.
rows.check: Later growth in confident incorrect predictions does not identify fitting of assigned noisy labels. It also matches the authors' proposed sequence rather than qualifying it as partial.

rows.subject: Standard
rows.operation_detail: Compared learned feature representations with noisy training labels superimposed.
rows.measure: Qualitative clustering in t-SNE visualization of the last layer before softmax
rows.value: Text states that feature representations are well clustered by noisy training labels and that Standard completely fits the noisy supervision.
rows.note: This is a qualitative result on noisy supervision, not a completely random labeling experiment.
rows.check: Final feature clustering provides neither a training-error measurement nor a temporal comparison for V6. Dataset attribution is inconsistent: the prose names 20 Newsgroups, but Figure 8 specifies setting 8, which Table IV assigns to TREC with symmetric noise 0.5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
